    AI Overview
    +11
    Response to Intervention (RTI) is a multi-tier educational framework used to identify and support students struggling with learning or behavior through early intervention and data-driven instruction. It provides increasingly intense, research-based interventions to improve student outcomes, often within a General Education setting. 
    Key Components of RTI: 
    • Universal Screening: Identifying all students at risk early.
    • Multi-Tiered System:
      • Tier 1:
        High-quality, differentiated classroom instruction for all students.
      • Tier 2: Targeted, small-group interventions for students not making sufficient progress.
      • Tier 3: Intensive, individualized interventions or specialized instruction.
    • Progress Monitoring: Continuously tracking student data to measure growth and adjust instruction.
    • Data-Based Decision Making: Using data to determine if a student needs higher-level support or specialized evaluation. 
    Key Differences: 
    • RTI vs. Special Education: RTI is a general education initiative designed for all students; it is not, itself, a special education program, though it can be used to identify students needing special education evaluations.
    • Goal: The goal is to provide immediate support to prevent long-term failure and bridge learning gaps. 
    Other Meanings: 
    • RTI International: A non-profit research institute.
    • Real-Time Innovations (RTI): A software framework company for autonomous systems.
    • Respiratory Tract Infection (RTI): An infectious disease.

    What is RTI in the USA?
    RTI is an independent organization founded by universities in North Carolina whose mission is to conduct innovative, multidisciplinary research that improves the human condition. RTI works in health and medicine, environmental protection, technology commercialization, education, and decision support systems.
